item.title: Police crackdown on illegal PMV protest in POM
item.description: Twenty PMV buses were impounded today and their drivers and crews arrested after staging an illegal protest over rising fuel prices, disrupting the city’s public transport system. Assistant Commissioner of Police and NCD-Central Commander Benjamin Turi personally led the operation, warning that police will arrest any PMV operators who overcharge passengers or engage in unlawful demonstrations.
item.content:encoded:
Twenty PMV buses were impounded today and their drivers and crews arrested after staging an illegal protest over rising fuel prices, disrupting the city’s public transport system.

Assistant Commissioner of Police and NCD-Central Commander Benjamin Turi personally led the operation, warning that police will arrest any PMV operators who overcharge passengers or engage in unlawful demonstrations.

“This is a warning to all PMV operators. We have impounded 20 buses and arrested their drivers and crews. If you overcharge passengers or stop work to stage illegal protests, you will be arrested. If you want to stop work, take your bus home instead of forcing others to join your protest,” ACP Turi said.

He stressed that fuel price decisions are made by the government and that operators must use proper channels to raise concerns rather than holding the city “at ransom.”

Turi highlighted the impact on school children, especially Grade 12 students currently sitting exams, who rely on PMVs as their only mode of transport.

The Commander also condemned the practice of buses failing to complete routes while charging multiple fares.

“We have buses charging K2 from Gerehu to Waigani, then another K2 to 4 Mile, and again K2 to town. That’s a rip-off unless you complete your route,” he said.

Police will now monitor bus stops to ensure compliance with fare regulations.

Turi reiterated that operators must abide by rules set by the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission (ICCC) and follow lawful avenues to express grievances.

item.title: Drought dries up Arokoi river in Kutubu

item.content:encoded:
More than a thousand people who depend on the main Arokoi river in the Kutubu area of Southern Highlands province are now looking for water for consumption following El Nino induced drought that dried up the river system.

The affected communities are Kaipu 1, Kaipu 2 and Sisibia 1, Sisibia 2 including nearby villages that depend on the main Arokoi river that provides for drinking, cooking and daily use by the people.

The villages also host the Kutubu Petroleum Development License 2 (PDL 2) PNG Liquified Natural Gas project.

Community Leaders Kenny Sasue, Justin Atakaro, Alexs Asi Ware, Freddy Daniel Boko and Gibson Sasue has expressed concerns, appealing to authorities about the impacts of the El Nino induced drought that is affecting their communities.

Kenny Sasue said Arokoi river is the main river that people rely on and also the PNG LNG project developers Santos and ExxonMobil use for the project facilities in the area and the prolong drought has really affected the river system.

“This is a big river that our people including mothers and children use for drinking, cooking and daily use for washing but with the dry season, it has dried up to a stream that it might dry up altogether in the next two weeks or after one month,” Sasue said.

“The small streams that we use to wash and filter our sago have all dried up and we don’t know where we will get the water for consumption after one month if the main Arokoi river dry up altogether”.

“We appeal to PNG LNG project developers Santos and ExxonMobil and to the government especially Prime Minister James Marape to hear our plight,” Kenny Sasue said.

“We also appeal to our local MP for Nipa Kutubu Dr. Billy Joseph for assistance as some of our people have died due to the impacts of the dry season” he said.

The community in the Kutubu area are among others nationwide facing the impact of El Nino induced drought.

The National Weather Service has warned that the El Nino peak is expected during the month of October to December and into next year (2027).

item.title: Call to regulate hire car rates
item.description: The Morobe Land Transport Authority has been urged to start regulating the hire car business rates in the province and also start issuing routes for new roads which have been constructed in the Wau Waria District of Morobe Province. Wau Waria MP, Marsh Narewec, said this after receiving complaints from his people, who travel and use the Kaindi Road, as well as the Northern Highway.
item.content:encoded:
The Morobe Land Transport Authority has been urged to start regulating the hire car business rates in the province and also start issuing routes for new roads which have been constructed in the Wau Waria District of Morobe Province.

Wau Waria MP, Marsh Narewec, said this after receiving complaints from his people, who travel and use the Kaindi Road, as well as the Northern Highway.

Narewec says that these roads were built and maintained by the National Government, for the ordinary people to use, but fast money-making people are abusing it, by charging exorbitant rates.

He also adds that not everyone in the district are alluvial miners, but they are still being forced to pay high fares and rates when using these roads.

Narewec has also called on the Land Transport Authority, to visit the district and allocate route numbers for vehicles, especially Public Motor Vehicles (PMV’s), who are currently operating on their newly constructed roads.

item.title: Waste management boosted
item.description: Port Moresby’s waste management capacity is set to improve with the 9.3 million kina newly completed Baruni Landfill Cell 3. This follows the commissioning of the third landfill cell at Baruni Dump in Port Moresby today.
item.content:encoded:
Port Moresby’s waste management capacity is set to improve with the 9.3 million kina newly completed Baruni Landfill Cell 3.

This follows the commissioning of the third landfill cell at Baruni Dump in Port Moresby today.

Waste Management Manage John Navara days cells one and two are almost full, and the development of the third cell is essential to maintain continuous waste disposal for the city.

Navara says the new landfill cell has estimated capacity of 350 to 400 thousand cubic meters. The facility will support the city's waste disposal needs for three to four years.

He explains it is built with the Fukuoka Semi Aerobic Landfill system; a system designed to reduce methane generation, accelerate waste stabilization and minimise environmental pollution with technical assistance from government of Japan through Japanese International Corporation Agency through the JPRISM projects which commenced in 2012.

He says initial preparations and earth started in 2021 and foundation works recommenced in November last year.

The completion of Baruni Landfill cell 3 marks an important milestone in waste management services in the nation’s capital.

This is the third cell engineered waste disposal cell at Baruni which was completed in June and is commissioned today.

item.title: Minister calls for honesty in exams
item.description: Minister for Education Francis Kikin Siune has called on students, teachers, parents and school authorities to uphold honesty and protect the integrity of Papua New Guinea's national examinations. The Minister's call follows claims circulating on social media that the 2026 Grade 12 national examination papers have leaked, which the National Department of Education has confirmed are fake following
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Education Francis Kikin Siune has called on students, teachers, parents and school authorities to uphold honesty and protect the integrity of Papua New Guinea's national examinations.

The Minister's call follows claims circulating on social media that the 2026 Grade 12 national examination papers have leaked, which the National Department of Education has confirmed are fake following checks by the Measurement Services Division.

In a statement, he said national examinations must reflect students' hard work, knowledge and preparation, not cheating or attempts to gain unfair advantages.

He warned individuals and groups attempting to sell fake examination papers or facilitate cheating to stop, saying the Department has been asked to follow up and identify who is behind the claims.

The Minister said schools found engaging in examination cheating will face serious consequences including deregistration, students may lose their eligibility for certification, while teachers involved face disciplinary action including termination.

He reminded provincial education authorities, inspectors, supervisors and school administrators of their responsibility to safeguard examination papers and maintain proper supervision throughout the examination period.

With Grade 12 examinations underway and Grade 8 examinations approaching, Minister Siune urged students to remain calm, avoid spreading unverified claims and concentrate on completing their examinations.

item.title: October Parliament ratification
item.description: The National Parliament will resume this afternoon for one of its most important sittings yet in the country’s history. The October session is when the future of the Autonomous Region of Bougainville and its aspiration to secede Papua New Guinea as a separate independent nation will be debated and decided by the National Legislature.
item.content:encoded:
The National Parliament will resume this afternoon for one of its most important sittings yet in the country’s history.

The October session is when the future of the Autonomous Region of Bougainville and its aspiration to secede Papua New Guinea as a separate independent nation will be debated and decided by the National Legislature.

In August, Bougainville Affairs Minister, Manasseh Makiba had tabled results from the 2019 Referendum, in which 97-point-7-percent of people had voted for a separate independence from mainland Papua New Guinea.

The Referendum Result was also accompanied with the Melanesian Framework, developed from the Melanesian Relationship Agreement signed in June last year, and the Joint Consultations Report, which highlights all major dialogue and engagements between the National Government and the Autonomous Bougainville Government since and the agreed outcomes from each of those meetings.

The Melanesian Framework provides a practical and phased or sequential transition for Bougainville from autonomy to self-government and eventually independence, while retaining a close, peaceful and enduring relationship between Bougainville and Papua New Guinea.

The Melanesian Framework will however, only come into play ‘if’ the National Parliament votes in favour of independence for Bougainville.

Given the Speaker had approved a three-quarters voting majority to give effect to Bougainville’s independence aspiration, this means at least more than 88 of the 118 MP’s must vote in favour of the Motion which will ask if Parliament accepts the results of the 2019 Referendum.

In an information session with the mainstream media in Port Moresby last week, Chief Secretaries Ivan Pomaleu of the National Government and Kearnneth Nanei representing the Autonomous Bougainville Government, say it has been acknowledged that the independence issue is ‘ring-fenced’ only to Bougainville, and that the Melanesian Framework has been jointly negotiated and agreed on to provide a responsible and constitutionally guard-railed pathway that respects the role of the National Parliament and the wish of the people.

The National Parliament will be accorded an information session prior to the October sitting, where the Technical Team of the National Government will brief Members on the Melanesian Framework and the Joint Consultation Report now before the House.

It is still unclear when Parliament will take the historic ratification vote, however, it is certain that the Bougainville issue will be top among the agenda, where the House will debate the issue with reference to the documents tabled before it, before the actual vote can take place.

The Melanesian Relationship Agreement states that this current 11th National Parliament will have the duty to discharge the Bougainville agenda, seven years after the independence Referendum was conducted.

In their last meeting in East New Britain in June, the ABG had presented the National Government side with a document outlining Bougainville’s Final Position.

This document generally outlines Bougainville proposing moving into Self-Government by September 2027 and to make a declaration for independence three years later in 2030.

On its part, the National Government acknowledges that both sides would move to implement the Melanesian Framework only if and when Parliament votes YES in favour of independence, however proposes a return to further joint consultations if Parliament votes otherwise.

The ABG has not clearly revealed its next cause of action if Parliament fails to vote in favour of independence.

It is however, pursuing two other simultaneous pathways to secure independence for Bougainville, apart from the Ratification process outlined under the Peace Agreement which has been running for over twenty years.

These processes include writing its own Constitution – a precedence from Papua New Guinea itself, as well as lobbying international support in recognition of its cause.

item.title: Education Secretary dismisses claims of Grade 12 exam paper leakage
item.description: The National Department of Education has dismissed claims circulating on social media that the 2026 Grade 12 national examination papers have leaked. Secretary for Education Dr Uke Kombra confirmed that the papers shared online are fake.
item.content:encoded:
The National Department of Education has dismissed claims circulating on social media that the 2026 Grade 12 national examination papers have leaked.

Secretary for Education Dr Uke Kombra confirmed that the papers shared online are fake.

Dr Kombra said the Measurement Services Division (MSD), which oversees national examinations, has checked the images circulating online and confirmed that they do not contain genuine examination papers.

"The security of examinations, from question writing to printing and distribution to the provinces is well secured, and any leak during this period is almost impossible. I want to encourage the public and education authorities not to panic but to remain vigilant," Dr Kombra said.

The Secretary urged students and parents not to fall prey to rogue groups or criminals selling fake examination papers for money.

He warned that the Department has systems in place to identify whether cheating has occurred.

“Examinations will be declared null and void if a school is caught cheating. Students will not be certificated, and teachers involved will be terminated," Dr Kombra said.

Dr Kombra stressed that provincial education authorities, Provincial Education Advisers, inspectors, examination supervisors and school administrators must take responsibility for securing examination papers once schools receive them.

He said MSD continues to monitor information, analyse reports and investigate possible breaches to protect the integrity of national examinations.

The Department confirmed that Grade 10 examinations concluded last week without major issues. Grade 12 examinations continue on Monday, October 12, while Grade 8 examinations begin next week.

The Department urges students to remain calm, focus on their examinations and avoid sharing unverified information online, and to rely only on official Department updates.

item.title: Medical screening and registration for police reservist underway in Northern
item.description: The Oro Provincial Government, through its administration, has funded K1 million to train young men and women as Police Reservists in the province. This has been confirmed to NBC News by Provincial Police Commander, Chief Inspector Charles Winuwan.
item.content:encoded:
The Oro Provincial Government, through its administration, has funded K1 million to train young men and women as Police Reservists in the province.

This has been confirmed to NBC News by Provincial Police Commander, Chief Inspector Charles Winuwan.

Winuwan, in an exclusive interview with NBC News, said the Police Reservists Program started some years back, but due to administrative constraints, the program has been delayed until 2026.

PPC Winuwan said the current recruitment of Police Reservists is comprised of those who completed Grade 12 between the year 2020 and 2025 and public servants. The medical screening, mandatory briefing, and registration process for the shortlisted Police Reservists' candidates commenced today and will end on Friday, 16th October 2026.

The medical examination will determine the final selection process of the Police Reservists' program.

On this note, PPC Winuwan said the shortlisted Police Reservists' candidates will undergo 6 weeks of intensive training at University of Natural Resources or UNRE Oro Campus and will be certified to conduct policing duties as reservists in the province.

In the meantime, PPC Winuwan pointed out that those who graduate as certified Police Reservists will be engaged in the upcoming National General Election in 2027.

PPC Winuwan thanked Northern Governor Gary Juffa with his administration to ensure the Police Reservists Program is delivered in the province going forward.
